title: socketcan: fix CAN packet type detection
description:
Existing DLT_CAN_SOCKETCAN implementations might use the optimized data length
approach where the frame length is not set to 16 for CAN CC resp 72 for CAN FD.
In these cases the frame size is cropped to contain only the needed data bytes
without any padding to 16/72 bytes.

This patch re-enables the optimized data length support.

Fixes: d3dd050c6a1a ("socketcan: simplify CAN packet type detection")
Signed-off-by: Oliver Hartkopp <socketcan@hartkopp.net>

notes.body:
> Existing DLT_CAN_SOCKETCAN implementations might

And existing non-pcap/pcapng non-SocketCAN logging file formats might, too; BLF is one of them.

Are you fine with the patch or are there still open questions regarding the performed tests to detect the different CAN frame types?

After the frame is definitely no CAN XL frame the initial check for CAN FD 
"if ((tvb_repif ((tvb_reported_length(tvb) == 72) || (canfd_flags & CANFD_FDF))"
looks a bit weird - but it catches either content that has the CANFD_FDF frame set and also CAN FD frames with the correct frame size of 72 byte that misses the CANFD_FDF bit.
And after that detection the possible frame sizes are proved.

When CAN frames are generated by the Linux kernel (e.g. in the CAN drivers that are using alloc_can_skb()), the entire struct is zero initialized:
https://elixir.bootlin.com/linux/v2.6.36/source/drivers/net/can/dev.c#L460
And this is true for all CAN CC/FD/XL drivers.

When you create the content of CAN frames in the user space and send it to the kernel via CAN_RAW or PF_PACKET sockets the user might pass uninitialized content to the kernel.
But Linux is only looking at defined values, flags and structure lengths. So it could be that you see uninitialized content when you read CAN frames - which is then caused by user space applications.

And I would like to see such uninitialized stuff in Wireshark as it points me to some application misbehavior.

Edit: This uninitialized user space data problem can not be fixed. Of course we could think of doing some sanitizing in CAN_RAW sockets - but there is no way to do this with PF_PACKET sockets.

Edit2: And this is also the reason why I suggested to remove the extensive sanitizing of 'uninitialized' content in my libpcap pull request: https://github.com/the-tcpdump-group/libpcap/pull/1296
